reflection.review:
A measurement-heavy cycle testing the basin-limit hypothesis from cycle 2.

1. **cotengra reference rows (cap era)**: HyperOptimizer (greedy+kahypar)
   best-of-3 scored 41.97 (reg3_250) / 68.02 (sycamore_m20) vs our records
   39.90/61.51 — external SOTA hyper-optimization is ~2/~6.5 log2 behind
   under the protocol. cotengra-sa initially failed on sycamore in all runs
   — diagnosed as OUR adapter's cap-compliance bug, not cotengra weakness.
2. **Attempt 019** (draft, structure-guided sycamore sweeps): scored
   39.996/61.619, no records. All structured spacetime sweeps landed at
   sc 73–98 vs TreeSA's 53 — the 8×7×20 lattice's temporal and spatial
   extents are not graph-separated enough for flat fronts; TreeSA already
   realizes the ~53-wide cut. Hypothesis refuted.
3. **Attempt 020** (improve, population × λ-ramp composition — the
   pre-registered basin-limit test): scored 40.110/61.635, no records;
   local best 39.894/61.555. Gain < 0.2 on both targets → by its own
   criterion the move-set direction is DEAD.
4. **Objective change (user-directed)**: v2.1 pure tc, sc unbounded;
   cap-era board archived; sc-cap guard removed; references re-measured.
5. **Pure-tc board (best-of-3)**: treesa-inf 39.950/61.544 — identical
   plateau; unconstrained sc changed nothing (min-tc trees are low-sc
   anyway). cotengra-hyper 41.68/63.97. cotengra-sa (adapter fixed)
   ~40.00/62.05 — nearly closes the gap to treesa-inf.

Budget: 2/2 remaining attempt slots used (019, 020); authorized round
consumed. Overrides recorded: pure-tc objective change (STATE.md).
reflection.evidence:
- Frontier: 39.95 / 61.54 (ref:treesa-inf, pure tc), reproduced by two
  independent toolchains; nothing known beats it at 90 s single-thread.
- cotengra-sa ≈ frontier (Δ ≈ 0.05/0.5); cotengra-hyper ≠ frontier.
- Blacklist: structure-guided sweeps on layered RQC proxies (019);
  move-set/constraint-handling variations (020 closed the direction).
- Unknown: distance from the frontier to the true optimum — no lower
  bound exists yet. This is the highest-value open measurement.
reflection.literature:
The two-toolchain convergence matches the anytime-plateau picture in
[gray_2020_hyper]; the sc_target finding now reads as "aspirational
low-memory targets are harmful, unconstrained tc is safe" — consistent
with [kalachev_2021_multi]'s overflow-penalty-only design (β penalty
activates only above the cap, never below: exactly the one-directional
harm we measured). Lower-bound machinery for next cycle is catalogued:
PID/minor-based LB [tamaki_2017_positive, tamaki_2022_heuristic].
reflection.next:
Hypothesis: the 39.95/61.54 frontier is near-optimal; certified lower
bounds will show a gap < 1 log2. Batch (6 slots): 021 LB for reg3_250
(line-graph treewidth, minor-based); 022 LB for sycamore_m20 (line-graph
treewidth + lattice cut counting); 023 hierarchical-exact search, expander
flavor (coarsen → exact DP → expand); 024 hierarchical-exact, lattice
flavor; budget-scaling measurement of treesa-inf at 90/300/900 s (not an
attempt); 025 debug slot. Abandon hierarchical-exact if it cannot match
the frontier; if LB ≈ frontier, declare the instances solved and pivot the
project to write-up + new instance regimes.
